scope: Recheck open-source DXF peer contracts for explicit mesh and ACIS routes; refine versioned peer admission and operation-level native acceptance readiness.

method.kind: Static primary-specification, project-source/documentation, and public peer-report review
method.evidenceRule: A peer result is scoped to exact entity, file version, direction, route, and operation. Documentation and issue reports identify limits or failure modes only; they are not local reproductions or support qualification.

findings.topic: DXF peer version export is not general conversion
evidence: ezdxf describes itself as a DXF interface rather than a CAD application or version converter and warns that unsupported features may be ignored when exporting to a selected file version.
Its API models classic POLYLINE modes and separate MESH authoring, which do not imply that it can downgrade or preserve every entity across target versions.
findings.disposition: Pin exact source and target versions, literal entity identity, direction, and omission policy. Treat any explicit downgrade as a named lossy projection with per-source disposition; do not use unsupported-feature omission as evidence of local loss.

findings.topic: Explicit mesh families require distinct comparators
evidence: Autodesk's DXF references define AcDbSubDMesh MESH topology/crease/override fields separately from classic POLYLINE mesh and signed-index PFACE child records.
GDAL's project known-issues document lists MESH as unsupported and describes its 3DFACE OGR representation as outline-oriented.
findings.disposition: Retain separate MESH, SUBDIVISION, POLYMESH, POLYFACE, 3DFACE, and modeler-geometry ledger rows. A derived mesh/face/render projection is not native entity or B-rep parity.

evidence: ezdxf discussion #1295 describes one mesh-authored 3DSOLID accepted by MASSPROP but failing a Dynamo Boolean-intersection workflow; the maintainer characterizes ACIS support as basic.
The public discussion does not provide an independently reproducible payload, full software configuration, or confirmed failure cause.
findings.disposition: Treat this as an advisory failure-mode lead only. Record file opening, display, mass-property queries, editability, and Boolean operations separately, with exact producer/application versions and independently expected outcomes.

findings.topic: Carrier, graph, shape, and consumer outcomes stay separate
evidence: LibreDWG issue #1411 reports an R2013+ entity shell surviving while its AcDs-hosted ACIS payload is lost in a specific build.
This is a peer report, not a current-version retest or libdxfrw reproduction.
findings.disposition: Retain the existing source-handle-to-carrier/owner-to-output-to-consumer chain and require separate evidence for bytes, graph closure, shape construction, validity/metrics, and operation success.
